newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government seals shipyard holding group.
newsitem.headline: Polish government seals shipyard holding group.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday pushed ahead with the creation of a shipbuilding group to help the industry survive foreign competition, Finance Minister Marek Belka said.

Belka said the government, tired of waiting for results of talks among the group's would-be members, decided to kick-start the scheme by giving its 46 percent stake in the ailing Gdynia shipyard to the sucessful Szczecin yard.
Under the scheme Stocznia Szczecin SA, would also take control of a majority stake in troubled ship-engine maker H. Cegielski and possibly other firms, he said.
"The Szczecin-led holding group is the only institution in our shipbuilding industry credible enough to count on government credit guarantees," Belka told a news conference.
The Szczecin shipyard will subsequently buy Gdynia's new share issue, which may double its capital, said Szczecin's president Krzysztof Piotrowski.
Poland's state-owned Bank Handlowy will also hand over its 18-percent stake in Gdynia to Szczecin, Belka said.
"The process will mean the much-needed inflow of capital to Gdynia shipyard...and better management," he said.
Following the launch of free market reforms seven years ago, Szczecin was the only shipyard to undergo successful restructuring, enabling it to compete with the world's best companies.
Szczecin's Piotrowski confirmed earlier reports that his company would increase capital by about 20 percent this year to raise funds needed to buy stakes in Gdynia and Cegielski.

"There is more than 50 percent chance that the issue would be taken by the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development," Piotrowski told Reuters. He added the yard would also welcome other buyers.
An industry official earlier said that the EBRD was in talks on buying up to 25 percent of Szczecin shipyard for about $100 million.
Under an earlier plan, the shipyard holding was to group a big steel mill and a bank, but Piotrowski said it was too early to say whether these institutions would join.

In the Szczecin shipyard, employees now have 34.7 percent of shares, a group of four Polish banks has 30 percent, with 15 percent in the hands of Capital Group Ltd, nine percent owned by the management and 5.3 percent by small shareholders.
The treasury now has 46 percent of Gdynia. Among its other shareholders are the state-owned commercial Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA which has 20.5 percent of shares and Bank Handlowy with 18.7 percent.
